Before we start on the numbers, tell me a little about your background.
Of course. I joined the bank eleven years ago and I have worked with investments ever since.
And before that? How long have you been in this industry altogether?
Almost twenty-five years. I finished my degree in the nineties and I have never left the sector.
What do you specialise in?
Clients who invest outside Brazil. I have taken on about forty families in eleven years.
That is a small number. Deliberately small, I assume.
Deliberately small. How long have you been looking for somebody here?
I have worked with investments ever since.

We have kept in touch for years.

Before we begin, let me introduce the person who is going to run this account. He has been with the bank for eleven years. He joined us in twenty fifteen, from another institution in the same sector, and he has worked with investments for his whole career. He specialises in clients who hold money outside the country, which is exactly why he is in this room today. He looks after about forty families, and I want to be clear about that number, because it sounds small. It is small deliberately. He has kept it small so that every family gets a real conversation and not a report. Right. I will hand over to him and he will take you through the numbers.

I had been in the same job for six years when it happened, and I still think about that afternoon. There were eight people in the room and one of them asked me a question in English. It was not a difficult question. I understood every word of it. And nothing came out. Four seconds of silence, which is a very long time, and then a colleague answered it for me, kindly, which somehow made it worse. I went home that evening and I did not tell anybody. Ever since, I have spoken in every meeting, even when the sentence is short and imperfect and I know it is not elegant. Nobody has ever complained about my grammar. They complained, for six years, about my silence.
